section_1.title: Introduction to 'Willa the Windmill'
section_1.content: Introduce the setup: A set of 'S' points on a plane. A character, 'Willa the Robot', holds a long straight laser beam (the line L). The line starts at a point P and rotates clockwise. When the line hits another point Q, that point Q becomes the new pivot point (the center of rotation), and the line continues to rotate.
section_1.example: Visual: A scattering of 5 dots (seeds) on a screen. Willa stands at one dot, her laser beam rotating like a clock hand. As it hits a second dot, the 'glow' transfers to that dot, and the beam keeps spinning.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Discrete vs. Continuous Motion
section_2.content: Explain the concept of a 'Pivot Switch'. Ensure the audience understands that the line's angle changes continuously, but the center of rotation changes at discrete moments (collisions). Explain that no three points are collinear to keep the transitions clean.
section_2.example: Graphic: A side-by-side comparison. A standard clock (fixed center) vs. the 'Windmill' (center jumping from a blue dot to a red dot as the line sweeps across).

section_3.title: The Magic Invariant: The Balancing Act
section_3.content: Introduce the 'k-points' concept. If there are 'n' points total, the line divides the rest of the points into two sets. Crucially, when the line rotates and hits a point, the number of points on either side of the line remains constant (except for the pivot point itself).
section_3.example: Visual: Highlight 2 points in blue on the left of the line and 2 points in red on the right. As the line rotates 180 degrees and swaps pivots, show that there are always 2 points on each side, maintaining a '2-2 balance'.

section_4.title: The 180-Degree Flip
section_4.content: Demonstrate what happens when the line rotates exactly 180 degrees. Since the 'k-points' on the left must now be on the right (because the line has flipped its orientation), every point must have acted as a pivot at least once to allow the sets to 'permute'.
section_4.example: Character Example: Willa starts with a 'North' pointing arrow on her head. After the beam rotates 180 degrees, her arrow points 'South'. To achieve this 'flip' while keeping the side-count constant, the line must have passed through every single point.

section_5.title: Summary and the Eternal Cycle
section_5.content: Conclude that the windmill process is periodic. Because there are a finite number of points and directions, the system will eventually return to its original state, proving that the 'Windmill' will visit every point infinitely often.
section_5.example: Animation: Speed up the rotation. Watch as the laser traces a complex web connecting all dots, eventually returning to the starting point and starting the exact same pattern again.

section_1.title: Introduction to 'Willa the Windmill'
section_1.content: Introduce the setup: A set of 'S' points on a plane. A character, 'Willa the Robot', holds a long straight laser beam (the line L). The line starts at a point P and rotates clockwise. When the line hits another point Q, that point Q becomes the new pivot point (the center of rotation), and the line continues to rotate.
section_1.example: Visual: A scattering of 5 dots (seeds) on a screen. Willa stands at one dot, her laser beam rotating like a clock hand. As it hits a second dot, the 'glow' transfers to that dot, and the beam keeps spinning.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Discrete vs. Continuous Motion
section_2.content: Explain the concept of a 'Pivot Switch'. Ensure the audience understands that the line's angle changes continuously, but the center of rotation changes at discrete moments (collisions). Explain that no three points are collinear to keep the transitions clean.
section_2.example: Graphic: A side-by-side comparison. A standard clock (fixed center) vs. the 'Windmill' (center jumping from a blue dot to a red dot as the line sweeps across).

section_3.title: The Magic Invariant: The Balancing Act
section_3.content: Introduce the 'k-points' concept. If there are 'n' points total, the line divides the rest of the points into two sets. Crucially, when the line rotates and hits a point, the number of points on either side of the line remains constant (except for the pivot point itself).
section_3.example: Visual: Highlight 2 points in blue on the left of the line and 2 points in red on the right. As the line rotates 180 degrees and swaps pivots, show that there are always 2 points on each side, maintaining a '2-2 balance'.

section_4.title: The 180-Degree Flip
section_4.content: Demonstrate what happens when the line rotates exactly 180 degrees. Since the 'k-points' on the left must now be on the right (because the line has flipped its orientation), every point must have acted as a pivot at least once to allow the sets to 'permute'.
section_4.example: Character Example: Willa starts with a 'North' pointing arrow on her head. After the beam rotates 180 degrees, her arrow points 'South'. To achieve this 'flip' while keeping the side-count constant, the line must have passed through every single point.

section_5.title: Summary and the Eternal Cycle
section_5.content: Conclude that the windmill process is periodic. Because there are a finite number of points and directions, the system will eventually return to its original state, proving that the 'Windmill' will visit every point infinitely often.
section_5.example: Animation: Speed up the rotation. Watch as the laser traces a complex web connecting all dots, eventually returning to the starting point and starting the exact same pattern again.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet Willa and her rotating laser beam line.",
            "She starts at an initial point on the plane.",
            "The beam rotates clockwise around this pivot point.",
            "When hitting another point, the pivot immediately switches.",
            "This creates the \"Windmill\" motion through the points."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout("Introduction to 'Willa the Windmill'", lecture_lines)
        
        # Points positions (A1-F6 grid)
        # Choosing spread out positions
        pos_p = self.grid['C2']
        pos_q = self.grid['D5']
        pos_others = [self.grid['A4'], self.grid['B6'], self.grid['F1']]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in 5 white points (#FFFFFF) at random positions. Label one 'P'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        dot_p = Dot(pos_p, color=WHITE)
        dot_q = Dot(pos_q, color=WHITE)
        dots_others = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=WHITE) for pos in pos_others])
        all_dots = VGroup(dot_p, dot_q, dots_others)
        
        label_p = Text("P", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(all_dots), FadeIn(label_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # She starts at an initial point. Draw a yellow line (#FFFF00) passing through point 'P'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pivot tracking
        pivot_tracker = Dot(pos_p).set_opacity(0)
        self.add(pivot_tracker)
        
        # Angle tracker (initial angle: 60 degrees)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(60 * DEGREES)
        
        # Laser beam line
        laser_line = Line(color="#FFFF00")
        
        def laser_updater(mob):
            p = pivot_tracker.get_center()
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            # Extend line far enough to cover the grid
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(p - 5 * direction, p + 5 * direction)
        
        laser_line.add_updater(laser_updater)
        
        self.play(Create(laser_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The beam rotates clockwise around this pivot point.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate target angle to hit Q
        vec_pq = pos_q - pos_p
        # Clockwise rotation: angle decreases
        # Current angle is 60 deg. 
        # Target angle for Q (from P)
        target_angle = np.arctan2(vec_pq[1], vec_pq[0])
        
        # Ensure we rotate clockwise (angle decreases)
        if target_angle > angle_tracker.get_value():
            target_angle -= 2 * PI
            
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # When hitting another point, the pivot immediately switches.
        # Flash Q yellow.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        label_q = Text("Q", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(dot_q, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            dot_q.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.5),
            FadeIn(label_q)
        )
        self.play(dot_q.animate.scale(1/1.5))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Change 'P' to white and set the green color (#2ECC71) to 'Q' as the new pivot.
        # Continue rotation.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            dot_p.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            dot_q.animate.set_color("#2ECC71"),
            pivot_tracker.animate.move_to(pos_q)
        )
        
        # Continue rotating clockwise (further decrease angle)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.increment_value(-60 * DEGREES), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # The line
        line = Line(start=LEFT*2.5, end=RIGHT*2.5, color=COLOR_LINE)
        line.move_to(p1_pos)
        
        # Angle tracker
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Line updater - rotates around a specific point
        # Using a mutable list to hold the pivot since functions in updaters close over variables
        pivot_data = [p1_pos]
        line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(pivot_data[0]))

        self.play(Create(dashed_line))

        self.play(Create(red_x))
        self.wait(2)

        self.wait(1)
